ground_truth: labels_sidecar.json, already present for all 1820 structures
wyckoff: OUT OF SCOPE — not in the sidecar, would be new labelling
verdict: D1 HOLDS FOR THE ORACLE: it stays at 0.9429-0.9524 on ALL FOUR labels, so the identifiability result is not specific to crystal system and the ceiling argument generalises to space group. D3 PARTLY HOLDS: the shape-free floor degrades 0.5286 -> 0.4048, so size-and-density regularities carry less on finer labels, but never collapse to chance. The RF degrades most (0.8952 -> 0.6810), which is the informative part: the cell metric determines crystal system almost fully but NOT space group, because space group needs the ATOM POSITIONS the metric does not encode.

monotonicity.oracle: NOT monotone in granularity (0.9524/0.9429/0.9524/0.9429) — flat, because spglib reads the reconstruction exactly and the reconstruction is either right or wrong
monotonicity.rf_lattice19: bravais 0.9095 EXCEEDS crystal system 0.8952 — 13 of 14 classes present and centering is partly metric-determined; then falls sharply to 0.7143 and 0.6810

macro_f1_withheld: space group has 18 singleton classes of 44 present (230 possible), and point group 3 of 21, so macro-F1 is degenerate on the finer labels and is NOT reported, per the pre-registration. Micro accuracy plus classes-present is reported instead.
chance_note: majority-class rate and 1/n_classes diverge hugely on the finer labels (space group 0.1095 vs 0.0043); both are reported because quoting 1/230 alone would understate the trivial baseline sixfold
defect_found_and_fixed: my first oracle pass derived Bravais from get_lattice_type()[0] and got 0.7571 — NON-MONOTONE against space group at 0.9429, which is impossible since Bravais is coarser. The cause was my derivation, not the oracle: labels.py maps CRYSTAL SYSTEM to a family letter (trigonal -> 'h') and appends the centering from the space-group symbol. Rerun with the pipeline's own bravais_lattice() gives 0.9429. The impossible ordering is what caught it.
